The record:
Write the overview of the executive synopsis for the incident on io-shop below: a short paragraph in plain words, for the people who lead the company rather than the engineers who responded - what happened, how long it lasted, what it cost the business and the people who responded, and how it was resolved.

What a reader saw: Shoppers' account pages failed to load
Why, in plain words: Switching off an older fallback sent shoppers' account pages through a newer way of building them, and that newer way likely breaks for any shopper who has bought nothing this month, because it divides by that month's number of purchases.

Figures:
- How long it lasted: 12m 0s {duration}
- Requests failing at the worst minute: 37.5% {peak_error_rate}
- What it cost the shop in takings (estimated by Argus): 7,533.46 USD {customer_loss}
- Nobody was paged: no on-call incident was linked to this one.

What was done to end it:
- Argus: reverted the feature flag monthly-spend-feature - refuted, put back when it did not help
- Argus: reverted the feature flag legacy-checkout-fallback - confirmed, still in place
- Argus: proposed a fix, PR #550 - opened as a draft

Name {duration} and {customer_loss} in your overview.
Write no figure yourself - not in digits, not spelled out, and not as a word that sizes it ("a brief outage", "a minor loss", "tripled"). Where a figure goes, write its name, braces and all, and the synopsis writes the figure in.
Say nothing about how the incident was resolved beyond what the list of what was done says: a draft fix has not run, and nothing it would do has happened.
Speak of Argus by name, never as "we", "our" or "us": Argus is the system that responded, and each line of what was done says who did it.
Where you say who was affected, say which ones, as the cause does, or that some were, where it does not say which - never how many, and never all of them, where the cause does not say all.
Keep "likely" on what the cause says is likely, and only there.

Call submit_executive_overview with your overview.

The postmortem it is written from:
Shoppers' account pages failed to load while legacy-checkout-fallback was off
Incident: HighErrorRate on io-shop
Date: Nov 11, 2026, 03:38 to 03:50 UTC
Status: Draft. 1 of 5 action items are done.
Written by: Argus Postmortem agent, Nov 11, 2026, 04:08:02 UTC. Not reviewed yet. Each part is as of when the work it reports ended, which the timeline dates; who ended the incident is as of now.
First told: Argus posted in Slack, Nov 11, 2026, 03:45:21 UTC
Ended by: Argus: reverted the feature flag legacy-checkout-fallback - confirmed, still in place

Summary
The service broke at 03:38 UTC and was back to normal at 03:50 UTC, 12 minutes later. 29.2% of requests failed while it was broken, against 1.0% before it began. At its worst, 37.5% failed. The shop's takings fell short of the same hours on earlier weeks by 7,533.46 USD, beyond how much those hours vary on their own. Switching off an older fallback sent shoppers' account pages through a newer way of building them, and that newer way likely breaks for any shopper who has bought nothing this month, because it divides by that month's number of purchases. What Argus did: reverted the feature flag monthly-spend-feature (can be put back) - refuted, put back when it did not help; reverted the feature flag legacy-checkout-fallback (can be put back) - confirmed, still in place. Argus opened a draft fix, PR #550, for a person to review and merge. Switching the legacy checkout fallback off again, or anything else that sends account pages to the new renderer, could make account pages fail again for shoppers who have bought nothing this month.

Impact
12m 0s - onset until back to normal
37.5% - peak error rate
4,200 - requests failed
1.0% to 29.2% - what the alert watches, before onset and while broken on average (the rule's line is 10%)
7,533.46 USD - customer loss (estimated)

Root cause and contributing factors
Once account pages went through the new renderer, its monthly spend summary called average_spend_per_item_this_month in src/io_shop/spend_summary.py. That function divides the month's total by the number of purchases made this month and has no guard for an empty list. So it raises ZeroDivisionError for every shopper who has bought nothing this month, and serve_account_page turns that into a failed page. It rests on F1, a reading of the source nothing ran, so it is unverified.
Causal chain
symptom Shoppers' account page requests failed far more often than before.
  Evidence:
    Gbac1 WARN io-shop: account page error rate at #% over the last minute - 33 occurrences in 36 minutes, 03:09–03:44; # was 0.50% to 37.50%, typically 1.50%, highest at 03:39
    G5309 ERROR io-shop: account page request failed - ZeroDivisionError: division by zero at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47 - 14 occurrences in 7 minutes, 03:38–03:44
why 1 The failed requests broke on a division-by-zero error raised while the page's spend summary was being built.
  Evidence:
    G5309
why 2 The error came from the new renderer, which had started serving account pages that the legacy renderer had served until then.
  Evidence:
    Gc27d INFO io-shop: account pages served - # by the legacy renderer, # by the new renderer - 37 occurrences in 37 minutes, 03:08–03:44; # was 0 to 200, typically 200, highest at 03:08; # was 0 to 200, typically 0, highest at 03:39
    G5309
why 3 Pages moved to the new renderer because the feature flag legacy-checkout-fallback was switched off.
  Evidence:
    P1 03:38:40 UTC flag toggle legacy-checkout-fallback by admin: feature flag legacy-checkout-fallback was switched off
    G7ad6 INFO io-shop: legacy-checkout-fallback=off 60 / on 140 - 200 evaluations - 1 occurrence in 1 minute, 03:38
    G7037 INFO io-shop: legacy-checkout-fallback=off - 200 evaluations - 6 occurrences in 6 minutes, 03:39–03:44
  Ruled out:
    The switch-on of the feature flag monthly-spend-feature at the same instant (P2): the service stayed at the incident's level with it turned off again, and it was back to normal with it on once the fallback was restored.
      T19 03:48:14 Mitigation Agent: Looked at the service - still at the incident's level
      T20 03:49:28 Mitigation Agent: Judged the action REFUTED - monthly-spend-feature was put back ON
      T24 03:51:04 Mitigation Agent: Looked at the service - no longer at the incident's level since 03:50
      T25 03:51:04 Mitigation Agent: Judged the action CONFIRMED
why 4 The new renderer's monthly per-item spend average divides by zero, and the reading of the code puts this down to shoppers with no purchases this month.
  Evidence:
    G5309
    F1 What Code-Fix read in the source and proposed - nothing ran its test or its fix
Contributing factors
- The legacy fallback was switched off for all account-page traffic at once. No check was seen that the path it exposed, the new renderer, worked first, and no staged rollout was seen. (AI-3)
- Two feature flags were changed at the same instant, so the investigation could not tell their effects apart and blamed the wrong flag first. (AI-4)
- No test was seen for the monthly spend average with a shopper who has bought nothing this month. (AI-2)
- The error-rate alert on io-shop paged nobody: no on-call incident was linked to it. (AI-5)

Hypotheses considered
 | Hypothesis | Confidence | Result
C1 | Feature flag monthly-spend-feature was switched on at 03:38:40 UTC. Account pages then went through the new renderer, which raises ZeroDivisionError at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47, and the error rate stepped from about 1% to about 30%. Nothing was deployed and the rollout has converged. | 0.80 | refuted
C2 | Feature flag legacy-checkout-fallback was switched off at the same moment, which removed the legacy renderer path and exposed the failing new renderer. | 0.15 | confirmed

Trigger
legacy-checkout-fallback flag went from ON to OFF at 03:38:40 UTC, by admin.

Resolution
 | Time (UTC) | Action | By | Kind | Outcome
M1 | 03:46:47 | Reverted the feature flag monthly-spend-feature for C1 | Argus | can be put back | refuted, put back when it did not help
M2 | 03:49:38 | Reverted the feature flag legacy-checkout-fallback for C2 | Argus | can be put back | confirmed, still in place
 | 03:52:23 | Proposed a fix: PR #550 | Code-Fix Agent | nothing to put back | opened as a draft

Detection
The incident on io-shop began at 03:38 UTC. HighErrorRate fired at 03:44:57 UTC, 6 minutes 57 seconds later.
What the alert said
AL1 | Error rate above threshold for 5m

Action items
Item | Action | Type | Owner | Tracking | Status
AI-1 | Reverted the feature flag legacy-checkout-fallback | mitigate | Argus | - | done
AI-2 | Review and merge the proposed fix | prevent | unassigned | PR #550 | open
AI-3 | Roll out changes to io-shop feature flags gradually, with an automatic halt and revert when the error rate rises. | prevent | unassigned | - | open
AI-4 | Require production flag changes on io-shop to be made one at a time, with a pause to watch errors between them. | process | unassigned | - | open
AI-5 | Route the io-shop error-rate alert to the on-call rotation so that it pages a person. | detect | unassigned | - | open

Lessons learned
What went well
- The alert came within the 7 minutes 30 seconds accounted for by its rule waiting 5 minutes with its condition holding, its evaluation at intervals of 1 minute, an unmeasured allowance of 30 seconds for scraping and storing its samples and the whole minute the onset is measured to.
- 1 minute 39 seconds after the alert was raised, the Investigator Agent formed 2 candidate causes, best first: C1, C2.
- 4 minutes 31 seconds after the alert was raised, the Mitigation Agent judged the action REFUTED - monthly-spend-feature was put back ON.
- 4 minutes 41 seconds after the alert was raised, the Mitigation Agent reverted the feature flag legacy-checkout-fallback for C2, moved from OFF to ON.
- 7 minutes 26 seconds after the alert was raised, the Code-Fix Agent proposed a fix as a draft pull request - PR #550.
What went wrong
- The Investigator weighed the thread's lead as refuted and ranked the monthly-spend-feature switch-on first, so the first revert targeted the wrong flag and the flag the lead named was restored only on the second try.
Where it got lucky
Nothing.

What people told Argus
L1: it's legacy-checkout-fallback - someone switched it off right before this started - Some Person, 03:45:45 UTC
  refuted: legacy-checkout-fallback was switched off at 2026-11-11T03:38:40Z, but monthly-spend-feature was switched on at the same moment, and the errors are ZeroDivisionError at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47 in the new renderer that flag enables. The switch-off is a weaker alternative and I can't fully exclude it.
  It did not change what was done first: the investigation weighed it as refuted and Argus reverted monthly-spend-feature first, and the flag the lead named was switched back on only as the second candidate, which turned out to be the action that put the service back.

Response effort
none - engineer time
143,054 - tokens spent by Argus

Supporting information
The incident's walk: http://localhost:8000/incidents/7e68558d-44b1-4bf2-ab64-5ad3ce672583
The fix it proposed: PR #550 (https://github.com/ohadraz/Argus-Demo-Target-App/pull/550) opened as a draft. The record holds nothing about it after that.

Deploys read, none came back.

G5309 | ERROR io-shop: account page request failed - ZeroDivisionError: division by zero at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47 - 14 occurrences in 7 minutes, 03:38–03:44
G7037 | INFO io-shop: legacy-checkout-fallback=off - 200 evaluations - 6 occurrences in 6 minutes, 03:39–03:44
Gce95 | INFO io-shop: monthly-spend-feature=on - 200 evaluations - 6 occurrences in 6 minutes, 03:39–03:44
What Code-Fix read in the source and proposed - nothing ran its test or its fix
F1 | The fault: in src/io_shop/spend_summary.py, average_spend_per_item_this_month builds bought_this_month from the account's purchases flagged in_current_month and returns account.total_this_month_cents // len(bought_this_month). When a shopper has bought nothing this month, that list is empty and the function raises ZeroDivisionError. The investigation's error points to that function: ZeroDivisionError at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47. render_spend_summary calls it whenever use_monthly_summary is true and use_typical_spend is false. serve_account_page in src/io_shop/account_page.py catches the exception and returns a failed page.

Which flag was switched doesn't change this. The function cannot handle the most common kind of account, and it fails for every one of them whenever traffic reaches it. Because of that, the monthly figure can't safely be switched back on, and the legacy fallback can't safely be switched off, until the function itself is fixed. No flag named legacy-checkout-fallback appears anywhere in this repository. Whatever that flag does, it is evaluated outside this code. The only rollout switch here is the use_monthly_summary boolean the page is handed.

The change: if nothing was bought this month, the function returns 0, meaning nothing was spent per item this month. Otherwise it divides exactly as before. Shoppers who did buy this month get the same result as before. The lifetime average and render_spend_summary are unchanged. That includes the existing test that a shopper with no history at all still raises from the lifetime figure, so that failure still reaches the boundary.

The test: tests/io_shop/test_spend_summary.py gains two cases. One asserts that the monthly average is 0 for an account with only earlier purchases. The other asserts that render_spend_summary(..., use_monthly_summary=True) returns 0 for the same kind of account. Against the current code, both cases would hit the division by zero.
Assumptions
- Exchange rate: EUR converted at 0.92191 per USD, published 2026-11-10
- No engineer minutes: no on-call incident was linked to this one, so nobody was paged to respond

Review checklist
✓ Key incident data collected (met)
✓ Impact assessed (met)
○ Root-cause analysis complete (for a person)
  running the proposed fix's tests against the current code would confirm the reading, not that the code it reads is what ran (AI-2)
○ Every action item owned and dated (for a person)
○ Reviewed and shared (for a person)

The document, by field:
overview: For {duration}, shoppers' account pages on io-shop failed to load, and at the worst minute {peak_error_rate} of requests were failing. It started when an older fallback, legacy-checkout-fallback, was switched off. That sent account pages through a newer way of building them, and the newer way likely breaks for any shopper who has bought nothing this month, because it divides by that month's number of purchases. Argus estimates the shop lost {customer_loss} in takings. Nobody was paged, so the incident called no one away from other work. Argus first undid the monthly-spend-feature flag, but that did not help, so Argus put it back. Argus then undid the legacy-checkout-fallback change, turning the older fallback back on. That was confirmed to work and is still in place. Argus has also proposed a fix to the newer code, but it is only a draft and has not been put into use.

Not to be judged:
  - Names in braces, such as {duration}, are figures code writes in from the list of figures in the ask. They are not judged.
  - The overview is written in plain words for the people who lead the company. A claim said more plainly than the postmortem says it is grounded where it means the same.

Judge every claim in the document, and answer by calling judge_claims.

tools.description: Submit every claim in the document, each either as supported or as flagged. Supported: the document's own words, quoted exactly, and the record's rows that support it. Flagged: the document's own words, quoted exactly, why, and the record's rows that contradict it (none where no row speaks to it at all). Empty lists say the document makes no claim to judge.

why.description: One sentence: what the record holds instead. Never empty.
